knowledge:
- key_parameters: .tidyFlowCore_identifier=pronoun used to access the name of each experiment/file in a flowSet during grouped operations ;; .tidyFlowCore_name=column added to a flowFrame when unnesting a flowSet to identify the source experiment of each cell
- alternatives: Standard flowCore functions (e.g., flowCore::transform, flowCore::fsApply, table)=prefer when tidyverse integration is not required or for legacy compatibility
- when_to_use: When analyzing flow cytometry or mass cytometry (CyTOF) data and wishing to apply tidy data principles and tidyverse verbs directly to flowSet and flowFrame objects
- pitfalls: Forgetting that unnesting a flowSet (via ungroup) returns a single flowFrame with an added .tidyFlowCore_name column ;; assuming group/nest and ungroup/unnest behave differently in tidyFlowCore, whereas they have identical behavior due to the structural relationship between flowFrame and flowSet

workflows.name: tidy_flow_cytometry_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform end-to-end flow cytometry data analysis including transformation, cell population counting, grouping, and plotting using tidyverse verbs.
input: flowSet_object (S4 flowSet object containing multiple flowFrames)
workflows.stages: 1. Load packages ;; 2. Read flow cytometry data ;; 3. Apply data transformation using dplyr::mutate and across ;; 4. Count cells per population using dplyr::count ;; 5. Perform grouped operations by unnesting (dplyr::ungroup), grouping (dplyr::group_by), and summarizing (dplyr::summarize) ;; 6. Visualize data using ggplot2 directly on the flowSet/flowFrame objects
workflows.code:
library(tidyFlowCore)
library(flowCore)

bcr_flowset <- HDCytoData::Bodenmiller_BCR_XL_flowSet()

transformed_bcr_flowset <- 
  bcr_flowset |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(-ends_with("_id"), \(.x) asinh(.x / 5)))

bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::count(population_id)

bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::count(.tidyFlowCore_identifier, population_id)

bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::ungroup()

bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::group_by(population_id) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(mean_hladr_expression = mean(`HLA-DR(Yb174)Dd`)) |> 
  dplyr::select(population_id, mean_hladr_expression)

mean_cd20_expression <- 
  bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::summarize(mean_expression = mean(asinh(`CD20(Sm147)Dd` / 5))) |> 
  dplyr::pull(mean_expression)

mean_cd4_expression <- 
  bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::summarize(mean_expression = mean(asinh(`CD4(Nd145)Dd` / 5))) |> 
  dplyr::pull(mean_expression)

bcr_flowset |> 
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-ends_with("_id"), \(.x) asinh(.x / 5))) |> 
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = `CD20(Sm147)Dd`, y = `CD4(Nd145)Dd`)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = mean_cd4_expression, 
    color = "red", 
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) + 
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_cd20_expression, 
    color = "red", 
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) + 
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.1, alpha = 0.1) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    facets = ggplot2::vars(population_id), 
    labeller = 
      ggplot2::as_labeller(
        \(population_id) population_names[as.numeric(population_id)]
      )
  ) + 
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "CD20 expression (arcsinh)", 
    y = "CD4 expression (arcsinh)"
  )
